title: Korea Post says hackers using overseas IPs accessed Internet Post Office recipient data; 11만3,855 people (including corporations) in one day's data
date_note: Hankook Ilbo says Korea Post became aware of the attack around 10:30 on the 25th; the announcement came on the 28th (Korea time).
geo_basis: Korea Post is a national agency; the source states no city, Sejong assumed as seat of the agency
summary: Hankook Ilbo reports Korea Post said an external hacking attack using overseas IP addresses reached the Internet Post Office. The count of victims in one day's data is 11만3,855 people (including corporations), and Korea Post is still checking the full scope. Names, addresses and phone numbers were exposed, per the article. Korea Post reported it to the Personal Information Protection Commission and asked police to investigate.
plain: Korea Post says an outside hacking attack on its Internet Post Office exposed names, addresses and phone numbers. One day's data covers 11만3,855 people (including corporations); it is still checking the full scope.
exec: A national postal service reports an external attack on its online service; 11만3,855 people (including corporations) appear in one day's data and the full scope is still being checked.
action: Korea Post advises the public to be wary of texts or calls impersonating the post office, such as address-change requests or demands for extra shipping fees.

evidence.quote: 하루치 분량의 정보 유출 피해자 인원수는 11만3,855명(법인 포함)으로 파악됐다.

validation.note: One publisher (Hankook Ilbo) relaying Korea Post's announcement; Korea Post's own notice was not read.
